speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned sudden-onset vertigo; can you describe exactly what you are feeling and if you experience any nausea or vomiting?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: The symptoms you described—sudden vertigo lasting only 3 minutes with nausea and vomiting upon lying down—are highly suggestive of a specific inner ear issue. Have you noticed any recent hearing loss, ear fullness, or tinnitus (ringing in the ear) accompanying these episodes?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sudden-onset sensation of the room spinning. I also have Nausea, Vomiting, Dizziness.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is concerning. Did this episode happen only once, or have you had similar spells since? Also, do you feel any weakness, numbness, or trouble speaking at all right now?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: The patient is otherwise healthy with only a history of eczema. No prior episodes of similar nature. Social history: No significant social history provided.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). The clinical picture of sudden, brief (<1 min to 3 min) vertigo triggered by position changes (lying down), accompanied by nausea/vomiting, in an otherwise healthy patient, is classic for BPPV.
